safety.adminOnly: Only an administrator can change these settings. You can still read them.
safety.windowDescription: Scheduled scans only run inside this window.
safety.windowDescriptionInfo: A window that crosses midnight (for example 22:00 to 05:00) counts by its start day.
safety.rateHint: Lower is safer for old devices.
safety.exclDescription: Devices or networks Vedette never scans.
safety.exclLabel: One IP or network per line
safety.exclHintInfo: The Vedette box needs no line here: it is scanned only when you pick it.
safety.stopDescription: Stop scanning when a device stops responding unusually, so it does not hang.
safety.stopSwitch: Stop automatically when a device does not respond
safety.neverDescription: Applies to every scan and cannot be turned off.
safety.neverHeadline: No changes, no denial of service

never.exploit: Never plants a file, an account or a backdoor and never takes over a device.
never.exploitInfo: A check may prove a flaw by making the device read a file or run a harmless command such as id, and keeps the answer as evidence.
never.dos: Never floods a service with requests to bring it down.
never.brute: Never guesses passwords and never logs in with default ones.
never.write: Runs only checks a person has read and found to change nothing.
never.writeInfo: All but a few checks are GET or HEAD requests: no account, password, setting, file, record or mail is created, changed or deleted, and no service is turned on.
never.tags: Only uses kev templates that pass Vedette's own filter.
never.tagsInfo: Only nuclei templates of the kev group that pass Vedette's own filter are used; templates tagged intrusive or denial-of-service are dropped.

safety.neverLocked: Dangerous checks are removed from this Vedette build; there is no switch to turn them on.
safety.schedDescription: Scan periodically inside the time window above.
safety.changedElsewhere: Someone else changed these settings since you opened this page, so nothing was saved. The current values are shown again: check them and save.
safety.nextScannerDown: The schedule is on, but nothing runs while the vulnerability scanner is not available. Check the box's services.
safety.nextBlocked: The schedule is on, but nothing runs until the scan scope commitment is ticked under Settings, Scanning, Safety.

auto.title: Rescan when a new KEV appears
auto.description: Rescans affected devices within 60 minutes of a new KEV.
auto.descriptionInfo: When CISA adds an actively exploited vulnerability that has a safe scan template, Vedette rescans exactly the devices involved within 60 minutes and alerts you if one is affected.
auto.switch: Rescan automatically when a new KEV has a scan template
auto.offNote: Off: new vulnerabilities will not be rescanned automatically.
auto.offNoteInfo: Vedette still alerts you when a new KEV matches a device by product.
auto.caption: Auto rescan event log

cred.noHosts: No server can be added yet.
cred.noHostsInfo: A server must be in the inventory, approved, and inside the scan scope.
cred.title: Credentialed scan
cred.description: Deep-scan important servers with a read-only SSH account.
cred.descriptionInfo: Vedette then sees real installed package versions instead of guessing.
cred.how: OpenVAS runs in its own container, separate from the confirming scan. You create a read-only account on the target and give Vedette the private key.
cred.privacy: The private key is stored encrypted and never shown again.
cred.privacyInfo: Vedette only displays its last four characters and never exports it.
cred.prepareIntro: Run the commands one at a time. The account has no sudo rights.
cred.step1: Step 1. Create a key pair (on your admin machine)
cred.step2: Step 2. Create the account on the target
cred.step3: Step 3. Copy the public key to the target
cred.step4: Step 4. Install the public key for the account (on the target)
cred.prepareEnd: Then open the vedette_scan_key file (the private key, without .pub) and paste its content in the box below.
cred.caption: Servers scanned with an account
cred.testWaiting: Checking the SSH login to {{name}}… this can take up to a minute.
cred.removeBody: Vedette deletes the stored key. To scan with an account again you must add the key again.
cred.empty: No server is scanned with an account yet.
cred.emptyHelp: Prepare the target, then add the server below.
cred.pickHost: Choose the target server from the list.
cred.keyHint: Paste from the BEGIN line to the END line, or choose the file.
cred.keyHintInfo: The content is masked while you type.
cred.keyTooBig: The file is larger than 16 KB, so it is not an SSH key. Choose the private key file.
